raw_provider_output.summary: A public service advertisement for Denver Water that uses the visual metaphor of an empty billboard frame to urge consumers to practice water conservation by using only what is necessary.

observations.description: A large billboard structure is shown from a low angle, but the main display area is empty, revealing only the metal scaffolding and support beams against a cloudy sky.
observations.location: center and upper portion of the image

observations.description: A bright orange rectangular panel is mounted on the right side of the empty billboard frame.
observations.location: right side of the billboard structure

observations.description: The text 'USE ONLY WHAT YOU NEED.' is printed in large, white, sans-serif capital letters on the orange panel.
observations.location: upper section of the orange panel

observations.description: The 'DENVER WATER' logo and name appear in white text at the bottom of the orange panel, accompanied by a small water drop icon.
A city skyline with various high-rise buildings and trees is visible in the background beneath the billboard.
The billboard is supported by a thick, rusted metal pole.

claims.text: The advertisement's primary message is a direct call to action for water conservation, specifically to limit consumption to only what is essential.
The empty billboard frame functions as a visual metaphor for 'emptying' or reducing water usage, reinforcing the textual message through the absence of a typical commercial image.
The use of a stark, empty structure creates a sense of minimalism and focus, stripping away commercial noise to emphasize the simplicity and importance of the conservation message.
The presence of the city skyline and the specific branding of 'Denver Water' targets the local urban population, framing water conservation as a civic responsibility for city residents.
By subverting the expectation of a billboard to sell a product, the ad positions water not as a commodity to be bought, but as a resource to be respected and managed wisely.
